title: Scale Identification Skill (REVISED)
revision_note: Contains good warnings about tonic ambiguity and passing tones. Now explicitly treats tonic, mode, thaat, and local modulation as PROBABILISTIC context and PROHIBITS unconditional scale-fit correction.
purpose: Determine the key/scale/thaat as a PROBABILISTIC prior for labeling, never as a hard filter that rewrites observed pitches.
method: 1. Estimate the TONIC (root / Sa) — the note where phrases resolve and rest. Use evidence, not just frequency.
2. Normalize observed notes to pitch classes.
3. Read the interval pattern relative to the tonic.
4. Match against known scale formulas to name the scale/mode.
5. Map to a Hindustani thaat for LABELING.

probabilistic_context.rule: The tonic, mode, thaat, and possible local modulations are PROBABILISTIC hypotheses. Do NOT use the global thaat as proof that every observed note must belong to one seven-note set.
probabilistic_context.local_modulation: A song may modulate or borrow notes. The scale is a labeling context, not a hard pitch filter.
probabilistic_context.chromatic_notes: Genuine chromatic/passing/borrowed tones must be PRESERVED, not forcibly moved into the scale. Present a scale-relative (sargam) label while retaining the observed chromatic pitch.

pitfalls: The tonic is NOT always the most frequent note — it is where phrases RESOLVE.
Relative keys share pitch classes — use where the melody rests to pick the true tonic.
Passing tones outside the scale are valid — do not overfit to one out-of-scale note.
prohibitions: PROHIBITED: unconditional scale-fit correction that moves an observed pitch into the thaat.
PROHIBITED: treating the confidence-1.0 key label as certainty.
